candidates.title: Norfolk Southern to serve new Audi plant in Georgia
candidates.excerpt: MACON, Ga. — Auto manufacturer Audi will build its first U.S. factory at a Norfolk Southern-served site near Macon, Audi CEO Gernot Döllner and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp announced on Saturday, Oct. 24. The $4 billion facility will create approximately 4,500 new jobs. Construction is expected to begin in 2028, with full production of about 200,000 vehicles per year projected for 2031. The facility will be built at the Middle Georgia Megasite, a 1,500-acre property adjacent to the community of Fort Valley in Peach County and 25 miles southwest of Macon. Norfolk Southern’s Albany District main line runs along the north side of the property. The site, about 4 miles from Interstate 75, is 171 miles from the Port of Savannah and 98 miles from Atlanta’s Hartsfield-Jackson Airport. candidates.excerpt: Valenciaport recorded an increase in container traffic during September 2026, supported by stronger import and export volumes, although transshipment activity continued to weigh on its overall performance for the first nine months of the year. According to figures released by the Port Authority of Valencia (APV) on October 23, the port system handled 498,837 TEUs in September, representing a 5.48% increase compared with the same month in 2025. Total cargo throughput also increased by 2.05% to 6.6 million metric tons, reflecting stronger activity across the facilities of Valencia, Sagunto and Gandia. Exports of full containers rose by 5.68% during September, while imports increased by 11.68%. Meanwhile, full-container transshipment volumes declined by just 0.82% to 179,002 units, marking a more moderate decrease than the trend recorded over the first nine months. The BNSF main line was most seriously affected between mileposts 69.7 and 72.7 on Saturday and into Sunday. candidates.title: New York short line wins $11.2 million federal rail grant
candidates.excerpt: Ontario Midland Railroad has secured an $11.2 million federal grant to rehabilitate approximately 10 miles of track in Wayne County, New York, improving infrastructure that supports the region’s agricultural and manufacturing shippers. The Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project will replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight grade crossings, replace seven turnouts and remove three others. Work also includes ballast placement, tamping and track surfacing, according to an Oct. 19 announcement from the railroad and U.S. Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand. The award comes through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements, or CRISI, program. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. candidates.title: Autonomous railcar technology earns $16M federal grant
candidates.excerpt: Intramotev will deploy two autonomous freight railcars on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad as part of a project supported by a $16.2 million federal grant awarded to the City of Columbia. The Federal Railroad Administration selected the city for funding under its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program, according to the announcement. Intramotev will serve as the technology partner, deploying its TugVolt technology on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia. Operations will proceed in phases under an FRA-approved test program, beginning with remote switching at COLT’s Columbia terminal and advancing to autonomous freight service across the full mainline, including its public crossings. candidates.title: MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak
candidates.excerpt: MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak A flurry of new vessel orders by MSC and HMM has sent the container ship orderbook to new highs as demolition rates remain at basement levels. A further 28 container ships of more than 13,000 teu have boosted the post-2009 orderbook to a new high of 16.2m teu, 46.5% of the current fleet. An order for 20 ships of 24,000 teu by MSC at Hengli Heavy Industries in Dalian has taken the company’s orderbook for ships over 20,000 teu to 62 vessels. South Korean operator HMM has also penned an eight-ship order, worth around $1.5bn, with Hyundai Heavy Industries and HD Hyundai Samho for 13,000 teu LNG dual-fuel units. The newbuildings will be deployed on HMM’s Far East-India-Mediterranean service, said the company. Hapag-Lloyd said in a customer advisory on 16 October that fire had been reported on the vessel. “We have been informed of the incident by Seaspan, the head owner of the vessel, with whom we remain in close contact. Seaspan has confirmed that all crew members are safe and accounted for,” the German shipping line said. Nearby vessels were reported to have responded to a distress call and the crew of the Espirito Santos Express abandoned ship. The container ship is now adrift in the Atlantic.
